title: Wound smooth connected unipotent algebraic groups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Use affine algebraic groups and smooth geometric unipotence in the sense of [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure], and connectedness in the sense of [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $\mathbb A^1_k$ be the underlying $k$-scheme of the standard additive group [def-sc-gm-ga]. Then $G$ is called $k$-wound if it is affine of finite type, smooth, connected and unipotent, and every $k$-scheme morphism $f:\mathbb A^1_k\to G$ is constant with value in $G(k)$: there is a $k$-point $c:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ with $f=c\circ(\mathbb A^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k)$. The test map $f$ is not required to be a group homomorphism. The trivial group is allowed.

source.place: Brian Conrad, The structure of solvable groups over general fields (2014), Definition 2.1, printed p.10, and Remark 2.3, printed p.11. Online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf.
